title: Consistent AI art style
author: Roguelike-Engine103
selftext: Hey all! I’m having a lot of trouble getting gen AI tools to produce consistently styled art that I can use in a game like r/21stCenturyHack , what I mean specifically, is I would like wearable items like armor and swords to look the same on different characters, but it’s generally impossible with the prompts and then I spend hours afterwards in Gimp fixing and cutting layers out to make assets for ‘paper doll’ mechanics…any good tools or prompt suggestions from the community?

comments.author: kytheon
comments.body:
Nano Banana Pro can do this. Just start with a reference object (say a piece of clothing) and a person, then say: put this piece of clothing on that person. Next, use the same clothing image and the other character you want to put it on as references. And it'll look consistent. 

If you don't use image reference and say "man in hoodie" and "woman in hoodie" you're gonna get two completely different hoodies.

replies.author: Roguelike-Engine103
replies.body: Thanks I’ll have to give this a try… I was excited that Nano Banana is integrated into Adobe Firefly

replies.author: kytheon
replies.body: Just make sure to use "image reference"

comments.author: mike402
comments.body: Have you tried Ludo.ai’s image generator? You can take and asset and edit it with a prompt to make it look different

comments.author: Uriel_1339
comments.body: I'm working on this for Visual Novels. Already got it worked out for children book art. I won't promote here though so feel free to dm if curious!

comments.author: Sea_Advance273
comments.body: For ChatGPT image gen prompts I always provide at least one reference image, sometimes a handful, from previous images that have successfully captured the style I'm looking for. Once you get a solid "style Bible" of images you can always reference that in future prompts and results will be more consistent.

comments.author: Trashy_io
comments.body: reference image -> base prompt -> grade & iterate

comments.author: Chologism
comments.body: I'm using a game theme and style description, and using reference images with nano banana. Pro can use up to 13 reference images iirc. I built this into SpriteCook.ai to make it easier to do this on the fly

comments.author: SproutsJeremy
comments.body:
1. Nude/Base body 
2. Do a rough draft draw manually of the clothing you want in photoshop/gimp (doesn’t have to be perfect, takes 5 minutes)
3. Do img2img
4. Done
